title: Can white holes merge? Eardley lifetimes from exact null-shell crossing and their consequences for white-hole binaries
description:
A short paper with an interactive 3D browser simulation. White holes are unstable: matter falling towards one piles up outside the horizon and seals it into a black hole (Eardley 1974). Using the exact thin-null-shell model of Barceló, Carballo-Rubio and Garay (JHEP 2016), the paper writes the lifetime of a white hole of mass M exposed to a perturbation ΔM in closed form, τE = 4M[ln(M/ΔM) − 1 − ΔM/M] (G = c = 1), and shows that the energy escaping a late explosion is exactly M − ΔM/w, which follows the universal profile 1 − exp((Δt − τE)/4M); the rest stays behind as a black-hole remnant.

Taking the smallest physically available perturbations, the cosmic microwave background alone limits the lifetime to τE ≲ 250–410 M for masses from 10 M☉ to 6.5 × 109 M☉, and a single quantum the size of the hole gives the absolute bound τE ≲ 880 M. Compared with gravitational-wave inspiral, a white hole reaches merger only if it is first exposed at a separation of about 6–10 M or less, within the last few orbits before plunge. In a white-hole pair, the burst of the first explosion leaves the companion only 12–50 of its own mass units to explode before it is sealed into a black hole. Together with the time-reversed no-bifurcation theorem, which forbids two white-hole horizons from merging into one, these estimates indicate that white holes in binaries either explode, leaving black-hole remnants, or merge as black holes. The estimates rest on spherical symmetry and null shells and are not a substitute for numerical relativity.

The record contains the paper (paper/white-hole-binaries.pdf), the script that reproduces every number and figure (paper/compute.py) and the source of the simulation, whose white-hole pair and white-hole plus black-hole modes are timed by the paper's formula. Live simulation: https://pandakingpunc.github.io/white-hole-simulation/

The work was prepared with the help of an AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic); the author directed it and is responsible for the content.
